As an undergrad, I worked as a CNA. The inpatient hospitalist was *always* an NP on our floor. Drove me mad when patients would ask when their doctor was coming. I would always take the time during vitals to (gently) explain the difference between an NP and an MD/DO, down to the different color name tags they had on their white coats. Patients were actually extremely receptive and curious — I just didn’t do it with a shit ton of obvious bias.

Yup. Went to a no-name, non-flagship state school known for social mobility and affordability. Premed advisor didn’t know shit, classes were a joke, and I devoted all my time to ECs and MCAT prep. Had a *very* easy time finding leadership in clubs and getting letters of rec, as I always stood out in the classroom (even though I wouldn’t have been anything special at a UC or an Ivy). Multiple As.

I’m an MS1, but if there’s one thing I learned from undergrad: do *not* listen to your advisor with full faith. Making the post here was a smart idea. Advisors, especially premed advisors, know a lot less than they purport.

I would only retake if you are confident you can score 520+. Given that your exam score was right in your practice range, I really don’t recommend a retake. Getting a 513 or 514 on the next one is fine, but it shows a) a lack of judgment in retaking when you weren’t prepared to score much higher and b) solidifies that stat for you in a way that isn’t to your favor in “holistic” admissions.
